children: said Monday they agreed to form a partnership to boost production from tight and complex reservoirs on the Norwegian Continental Shelf that authorities believe have significant potential.

agreed to sell on a set of transactions in the Troll-Fram (Ringvei Vest), Yggdrasil, and Wisting areas, including the sale of a 19% interest in the Grosbeak, Rover Nord & Sor, Toppand, and Swisher discoveries to Aker BP
is the operator of Ringvei Vest, which is envisioned as a cluster development of multiple oil and gas discoveries in the Troll-Fram area of the North Sea.
also agreed to sell a 38.16% stake in the Frigg U.K. license to Aker BP
, enabling joint development of the Omega Alfa discovery and the Frigg Field oil resource potential in the area, and Aker BP agreed to pay $23M in cash to Equinor.
As part of the transactions, Equinor
will increase its ownership in the Wisting discovery to 42.5% from 35%, strengthening its position in the largest undeveloped discovery on the Norwegian Continental Shelf.

"By taking a portfolio-wide approach and developing common solutions, we can reduce costs and accelerate technology development... [which] can make more of these discoveries commercially viable," Equinor's
head of exploration and production Kjetil Hove said.
